title: appd interface review
stage: Contract preparation — new requirements not yet contracted
draftStatus: Every proposed signature and rule is awaiting approval

nodes.label: CLI / future dashboard
nodes.question: Which operations should both the CLI and dashboard reach?

nodes.label: agentguard daemon
nodes.question: The daemon entry point and the client-side start operation are separate call paths.

nodes.label: IDaemonService
nodes.question: Review these operation names, return types and cancellation shape. Start and stop report failure by exception; returning means the requested state was observed. That behavior is proposed, not approved.

nodes.label: IAutostartEntryService
nodes.question: Runtime and persistent configuration have separate owners in this candidate. Installation/removal stay with setup. The inspection result and further settings remain explicit design questions.

nodes.label: DaemonService
nodes.question: This is the wiring between the top interface and OS abstraction. Its method bodies are not being approved through this diagram.

nodes.label: AutostartEntryService + setup
nodes.question: Inspect the current ISetupCondition below. We must settle its synchronous boundary before introducing async setup work. Doctor must preserve an intentionally disabled entry.

nodes.label: DaemonHost
nodes.question: The approved stop command adds shutdown work absent from the recorded DESIGN. This diagram does not claim the old idle-loop design implements stop. Mutex ownership must survive the wait on the same thread; the earlier cancellation-linked await alone does not establish that.

nodes.label: IPlatformServices
nodes.question: One daemon property containing three capabilities, or three direct properties? The grouping selector changes the actual declaration shown here.

nodes.label: ISingleInstanceLock
nodes.question: Review nullable lease versus a dedicated result/lease interface. Lock paths are computed inside each platform implementation, not supplied by a caller. Windows release is thread-affine; the generic IDisposable lease must preserve the acquiring thread, or the host lifetime must do so. No threading mechanism is silently selected.

nodes.label: IDaemonProcessControl
nodes.question: Review one start/stop interface versus separate interfaces. The OS adapter derives the client scope. Windows session-targeted COM is proposed but not approved.

nodes.label: IAutostartEntry
nodes.question: The parameter/return shapes are draft C#, with unresolved DTOs clearly named. Launch conditions, retry settings and logging must be decided before these data contracts can be completed.

nodes.label: IAssemblyResources
nodes.question: The proposed resource service returns an owned IReadStream rather than raw Stream. Its Assembly reader and text-reader/bridge interfaces are now shown in the native layer. Review whether preserving the stream-shaped API is worth those extra wrappers, versus an explicitly composed text-resource service. Existing IBuildInfo is unchanged.

nodes.label: IPlatformFileSystem
nodes.question: The recorded DESIGN proposes a Windows throw, following MakeExecutable. Do we want that platform-limited operation or an OS-uniform contract? Do not silently infer Windows ACL behavior.

nodes.label: macOS adapters
nodes.question: Manual-start-only mode and stop must not accidentally re-enable login startup. Restart policy determines how this adapter manages the loaded job.

nodes.label: Linux adapters
nodes.question: Starting at default.target can precede the desktop. Graphical-session startup needs integration; a daemon started earlier needs an explicit later UI connection.

nodes.label: Windows adapters
nodes.question: COM replaces schtasks for explicit session targeting in this candidate. This needs approval, a mirrored native wrapper, and Windows multi-session proof.

nodes.label: Process + start options
nodes.question: Proposed owners: ProcessFactory creates AbstractedProcess; its StartInfo property exposes an AbstractedProcessStartInfo. Names and members mirror the BCL, with owned interfaces replacing actionable raw objects. The shared command runner uses these on macOS and Linux; Windows also uses process identity/session reads. Start/stop policy and timeout decisions stay above these wrappers. StandardOutput and StandardError are borrowed readers owned by IProcess; drain both concurrently before awaiting exit. Kill is for the launched service-manager command on cancellation, not a second way to launch or stop appd. SessionId is used by Windows, not as a POSIX daemon scope.

nodes.label: FileStream lifetime
nodes.question: Proposed owners: FileStreamFactory creates AbstractedFileStream, the sole raw FileStream owner. Dispose is the only operation needed on this lock handle; no read, write, path-discovery or unlink operation is added. Create mirrors the FileStream constructor. The lock adapter supplies OpenOrCreate, ReadWrite and None after computing the approved runtime path. The returned object keeps that open file alive; disposal closes it. Only the lock adapter interprets an expected sharing conflict as contention. Other I/O failures remain errors. This is a lifetime-only interface, not a missing implementation.

nodes.label: Mutex lifetime
nodes.question: Proposed owners: MutexFactory creates AbstractedMutex, the sole raw Mutex owner. Create mirrors the constructor; TryOpenExisting, WaitOne and ReleaseMutex mirror BCL members. Dispose closes the handle; it is not a substitute for ReleaseMutex. Acquisition and release must happen on the same thread. A lease held across arbitrary awaits cannot silently promise that. The host still needs either a dedicated owning thread or a synchronous owning lifetime. An abandoned mutex grants ownership while throwing AbandonedMutexException; that case needs explicit handling, not a false 'not running' answer. The wrapper does not choose the Local\\ name or decide what contention means.

nodes.label: Task Scheduler objects
nodes.question: Proposed owners: TaskServiceFactory and one Abstracted wrapper per returned COM interface, all in the Windows assembly. This is an owned C# review surface, NOT a COM ABI declaration. Connect selects local/current credentials. String/string-array parameters cover the needed BSTR and empty VARIANT cases; no object/dynamic escape hatch is proposed. Native flags retain their integer types; the appd adapter pins the allowed values. Collection indexing follows COM's 1-based index. Each returned wrapper is an owned reference disposed by its caller. Disposing a wrapper releases the COM reference; it does not stop the task. RunEx is the proposed replacement for schtasks, not an approved change. For stop, compare each instance's EnginePID session via IProcessFactory.GetProcessById, then Stop the matching instance. That selection is a candidate requiring Windows multi-session and process-exit-race proof; EnginePID is the task engine PID, not an assertion that it is appd's PID. COM activation, apartment handling and ABI marshalling remain an implementation-design review, not implied by these signatures.

nodes.label: Assembly resource streams
nodes.question: Proposed owner: AssemblyResourcesAdapter reads resources from the assembly selected at composition and returns an owned read-stream wrapper. GetManifestResourceStream mirrors Assembly's name and missing-resource null result; IReadStream replaces the raw Stream. The caller disposes the returned stream. The resource reader does not choose a template identifier, substitute placeholders or decide that a missing embedded template is acceptable. Template code makes missing data an actionable error. This replaces the old draft that leaked Stream. Existing IBuildInfo remains a version-metadata interface and is not extended for resources. StreamReader construction is shown in the separate Text readers node, including the necessary owned-stream bridge.

nodes.label: Text readers + bridge
nodes.question: Proposed owners: AbstractedTextReader is the one TextReader/StreamReader wrapper, shared by process output and resource reading. StreamReaderFactory uses the BCL decoder rather than rebuilding text decoding. Because that constructor accepts a raw Stream, an owned bridge is needed: ReadStreamBridge implements IReadStreamBridge and derives from Stream, forwarding Read to the supplied IReadStream. StreamReaderFactory obtains it through IReadStreamBridgeFactory; an internal composition-only conversion supplies its Stream view to the BCL constructor. That conversion and its analyzer allowance require review; it must never downcast an arbitrary IReadStream or fail for a fake. This added bridge is the visible cost of preserving both the Assembly stream surface and the no-raw-object boundary. Seek/write/length operations on the read-only non-seekable bridge throw NotSupportedException; they are Stream's abstract members, not new template capabilities. leaveOpen defines whether reader disposal closes the supplied stream. Process-owned readers remain borrowed by the command runner; their lifetime ends with IProcess. Alternative requiring approval: expose a composed ReadAllText resource service, eliminating the public stream/reader bridge but no longer presenting a one-for-one Assembly boundary.

nodes.label: Windows account identity
nodes.question: Proposed owners: WindowsIdentityFactory creates AbstractedWindowsIdentity; User returns an AbstractedSecurityIdentifier. These mirror WindowsIdentity.GetCurrent, WindowsIdentity.User and SecurityIdentifier.Value without exposing a raw identity object. The Windows autostart adapter derives the approved per-user task name from that SID. A missing User value is an error, not a fallback to a shared task name. The account SID and the process SessionId are different values and serve different purposes. The identity owner is confined to the Windows assembly.

ruleExamples.label: Own Process launch once
ruleExamples.good:
// One Process adapter in CrossPlatform;
// macOS and Linux invoke it through an owned interface.
ruleExamples.review: Windows COM reduces the Windows need for the shared command runner. Its owner still serves macOS and Linux.

ruleExamples.label: Own POSIX file locking
ruleExamples.bad: new FileStream(path, ...) // outside the lock owner
ruleExamples.review: Lease disposal must release the file handle; do not expose the raw FileStream.

ruleExamples.label: Own Windows mutex access
ruleExamples.review: The mutex owner and lease shape remain to be approved.

ruleExamples.label: No caller-supplied command or lock path
ruleExamples.review: Definition DTOs need inspection too; placing arbitrary commands inside a DTO would evade a parameter-only rule.

ruleExamples.label: Pin each operation to its caller
ruleExamples.bad: // Any unrelated Engine class calls the raw start port.
ruleExamples.good: // DaemonService owns start/stop; setup owns writes.
ruleExamples.review: The recorded text gives Detect to the setup condition, but the selected design also calls Detect from DaemonGate. Resolve that caller-table contradiction and add stop/configuration callers.

ruleExamples.label: Confine service-manager tool names
ruleExamples.good: // The per-OS adapter owns the fixed tool invocation.
ruleExamples.review: Entry writing also needs service-manager operations. The recorded start-owner-only allowance must account for that owner and the Windows COM proposal.

ruleExamples.label: Confine runtime-directory discovery
ruleExamples.good: // Both probe and acquire use the lock owner's path.
ruleExamples.review: Review each banned variable against existing legitimate consumers. A global HOME ban can exceed the lock-path concern.

ruleExamples.label: Constrain the macOS temp exemption
ruleExamples.good: // Suppression only on the approved macOS lock-path member.
ruleExamples.review: The full approved exemption must enter the contract. Attribute scanning alone does not cover every suppression mechanism.

ruleExamples.label: No broad exception catch
ruleExamples.good:
// Catch a specific expected lock-contention exception.
// Preserve other errors for diagnosis.
ruleExamples.review: This is a scoped proposal, not a general ban on every exception boundary.

ruleExamples.label: No mutable state in adapters
ruleExamples.bad: private bool isRunning; // cached OS state
ruleExamples.review: A lifetime lease legitimately owns a handle. Distinguish the lease from stateless adapters; do not ban the state the mechanism needs.

ruleExamples.label: Cover every interface owner
ruleExamples.bad: // A production service interface is unreachable and unregistered.
ruleExamples.good: // Container-reachable interface or explicitly governed native owner.
ruleExamples.review: The shared launcher and resource/COM wrappers require coverage. Internal interfaces outside Contracts must not fall through this rule.

ruleExamples.label: Use the injected clock for waits
ruleExamples.review: Example is schematic. Verify the actual timeout source and cancellation; async alone does not prove clock ownership.

ruleExamples.label: No idle polling loop
ruleExamples.review: The new stop operation needs shutdown signalling. This example illustrates the rule and does not select a shutdown interface.

ruleExamples.label: Pin templates to their identifiers
ruleExamples.bad: // Template and C# disagree about the task name or launcher.
ruleExamples.review: Use the approved Windows appd-<user SID> name, not the old constant task name in the recorded rule. Pin rendered definitions, including escaping.

ruleExamples.label: Require real per-OS adapter coverage
ruleExamples.bad: // Windows task adapter has only fake-based unit tests.
ruleExamples.good: // NativeSpec exercises the real adapter on its OS.
ruleExamples.review: Marker discovery must cover interfaces declared in Contracts. Include multi-session start/stop and disabled-autostart behavior.

ruleExamples.label: Pin presence-gated commands
ruleExamples.bad: // daemon prompts for presence on every login.
ruleExamples.good: // daemon stays ungated; existing install/init/remove stay gated.
ruleExamples.review: The new stop and autostart configuration operations need an explicit presence policy before this fixed verb-set rule can be approved.

policies.label: Recover on the next client request
policies.recommendation: Recommended for the first common policy
policies.reason: Same recovery semantics on all three OSes, with no background restart loop to fight stop or disabled autostart.
policies.decision: A crash leaves appd stopped until the next command needing it starts it through the OS service manager. Login startup remains enabled by default. This trades immediate unattended recovery for consistent behavior.

policies.decision: Proposed comparison values: 60 seconds, with three retries where meaningful. These settings are not an approved common contract.

logging.proposal: appd writes its own bounded log on every OS
logging.reason: Task Scheduler cannot redirect stdout/stderr in its executable action, so service-manager redirection cannot provide the same log on all three.
logging.draft:
Proposed location: ~/.agentguard/logs/appd-<scope>.jsonl
Proposed fields: time, level, event, message
Proposed limit: 5 MiB per file, one previous file per scope
Windows scope includes session ID; POSIX uses account scope.
No secrets, environment dumps or user-request payloads.
Location, schema, limit and reading command all await approval.
No total retention bound across expired Windows sessions is selected.
logging.question: Keep this common file log, or use each OS's native logging system and accept different viewing tools? No logger has been selected or built. Session-log cleanup and startup failures before the logger opens also need a mechanism.

blockers: Windows session-targeted start and stop are proposals, not approved replacements for schtasks.
Linux must connect appd's UI to the requesting client's desktop; startup timing alone does not settle that.

systemd documents support for only one graphical session per user. Reaching multiple simultaneous Linux desktops needs an additional UI connection/lifecycle design; the user unit alone does not provide it.
Autostart settings, retry policy and logging contents need approval before templates can be finalized.
Stop/configuration expand the recorded design; the original sixteen rules do not yet cover all of that work.
Current setup Detect/Repair methods are synchronous. The draft asynchronous entry interface needs an explicit integration decision.
The Windows mutex must be released on its acquiring thread; the current async lifetime sketch does not choose how to preserve that ownership.
